- Candidate deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest start), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), Private VPC/on-prem (data residency & PHI controls).
- MediMap preference on the call: leaning Private VPC because of PHI, but want cost and ops tradeoffs in writing.

As next steps, can you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow?
1) Primary requirement: data residency / PHI handling — is Private VPC a hard requirement for the PoC or acceptable only for production?
2) Success criteria: what are your concrete pass/fail metrics (latency P95, throughput, quality / F1 or human review pass rate)?
3) Tentative PoC window and stakeholders (procurement + infra + engineering) — include names and emails.

Attaching our short security questionnaire and a blank PoC-SLA spreadsheet to help frame the PoC. Once we get your answers, Ben and I will recommend an ops plan (hosted fallback, dedicated sizing, or Private VPC buildout) and a two-week pilot schedule.

Cheers,

Target kickoff: week of Mar 14, 2027 — 2 week pilot then 2 week stabilization. Stakeholders: Lina Torres (Eng lead), Jose Alvarez (Procurement), Dr. Mona Singh (Security officer, mona.singh@medimap.com).

Lina

Subject: Dedicated vs Private: ops recommendation + sizing notes

Hi all — adding technical detail to help you decide quickly. High level: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) gives most of the operational simplicity of Hosted with the data isolation controls you need; Private VPC adds more configuration & validation but is ultimately the most restrictive and compliant.

Recommend for the PoC: Dedicated with private peering + enforced no-egress policy. Fallback plan: short grace period where requests route to Hosted API for non-PHI traffic only.

Sizing notes:
- Expected concurrency: up to 50 concurrent requests @512 tokens.
- Baseline instance suggestion: 2 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) split across 4 worker processes for autoscaling; reserved throughput target = 75 reqs/sec sustained burstable.
- Batching policy: 8-12 token-level batching for cost efficiency; keep KV cache warm for repeat prefixes.
- Latency expectation: P95 ~ 160-220ms for 512 token requests with recommended batch config; P95 SLA request of <=250ms is achievable.

Operational asks for MediMap:
1) Short-lived test credentials for the PoC VPC peering test lane (we will not store keys after test).
2) A named security contact for SOC2 evidence exchange (Dr. Mona Singh listed earlier).

Attachments: redwood_poc_runbook.md (ops steps, smoke tests, rollback checklist).

If you confirm Dedicated for PoC I can send an ops ETA and a proposed canary plan (1-2 day canary then full 2-week pilot).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
